tagline: From an Army fort on the Carson over the Pine Nuts.
intro: The byway leaves Fort Churchill on the Carson River for Dayton, then runs into the Pine Nut Mountains past the site of Como and on by Simpson to Wellington, 67 miles in all.

The fort went up in 1860 after the Pyramid Lake War, to guard settlers and the Pony Express mail, and was abandoned in 1869. Its buildings went at auction for $750 after the state declined them, and the rancher Samuel Buckland salvaged materials from the dismantled fort for the two-story building that still stands at his old way station nearby.

moments.title: Fort Churchill
moments.text: Some 200 soldiers held this post through the Civil War, and its ruins are now kept in a state of arrested decay, with a visitor center the Civilian Conservation Corps built.

moments.title: Dayton
moments.text: Emigrants stopping at this bend of the Carson River had to decide whether to follow the river south or keep west, and the place was first called Ponderers Rest.

moments.title: Como
moments.text: A visiting correspondent in 1863 counted four hotels, eight saloons and a brewery in this Pine Nut Mountains gold camp, now a ghost town.

practical: Parts of the byway need a high-clearance vehicle.
